text: The Putus Templar lay siege to Grit Gate in a battle where the player must hold the enclave alongside the Barathrumites. The fighting carries the real risk of allied NPCs dying for good.

Having caught a strange repeating signal, Argyve sends the player to Grit Gate to consult Otho and Barathrum. It follows Weirdwire Conduit and serves as the player's introduction to the Barathrumites.
An aged mutant tinker of Joppa, a low-tier merchant and junior Barathrumite. He opens the story by building the Weirdwire Conduit and taking the player on as his apprentice.

A vain sentient plant of the Consortium of Phyta, who has crowned itself Earl of Omonporch. Weak in a fight, it is shielded by twelve asphodelytes, its followers, whose electrical powers make any assault deadly.
A robotic altar-being of the Temple of the Rock. It is the last functioning computer of its kind and it is revered as the "House of God" by the Mechanists

The eldest and wisest urshiib in Qud and head of the Barathrumites, credited with inventing the Barathrum clock and the astrolabe. He hands out the endgame quests and conceals a hidden bond with the Seraphic Covenant.

A secretive guild of tinkers, mostly urshiib, hidden at the bottom of Grit Gate behind an army of chromelings and waydroids. Led by their namesake Barathrum the Old. At odds with the Mechanimists who refuse using technology

A sprawling subterranean complex the Mechanimists hold sacred, enclosing the Temple of the Rock within its depths. The temperature gets lower the deeper it gets and holds various specimens in the cryogenic chambers
Strands of copper wire scattered through the Rust Wells. Although Although rare, it hold value only in the hands of a tinker. Needed to build the weirdwire conduit
Otho sends the player into the depths of Bethesda Susa and the Temple of the Rock to decode the mysterious signal, clashing with the Mechanimists along the way.
The mausoleum of the Eaters, accessed from the Omonporchl. Grave robbers infest the once sacred place.
The boss fighter role: a unique, high-level combatant set apart from common foes.
The non-boss fighter role: a capable combatant who is not a unique boss enemy.
Sentient fungi that spread by spore and infection across Qud.

Faction of various monsters which objective is to devour everything that moves. They are an existential threat to Qud's sentient life. Their slumbering Nephilim are among the great threats of the endgame. Beating them is necessary to save Qud.

The Girsh Nephilim are creatures of the seventh plague upon Qud. There are seven known Nephilim, the strongest being Starformed Ehalcodon. Once put to sleep by Reseph, they awake after a thousand-year-long sleep
A colossus built by the Barathrumites. It is the vessel by which the player ascends to Starfarers' Quay

A multi-level refuse pit choked with trash, sewage and deadly creatures, descending to the fetid Cloaca at its bottom. It serves as the Barathrumites' trial: here the player recovers a scrapped waydroid under the shadow of Slog.

A fortified Barathrumite outpost beneath an arch of jungle-strangled ruins. The heart of the enclave where Otho, Barathrum and the other barathrumites reside, it is where the main questline takes root.

The robotic keeper of the Eaters' Tomb, found beside Resheph's empty sarcophagus. He is bound up with the rite of entombment that grants acces to Brightsheol, a console that controls acces to Starfarers' Quay by modulating the magnetic field
The starting village on the surface, raised on stilts amid fields of watervine. Home to the tinker Argyve and the launch point for the player, it is the first safe haven a new wanderer comes to know.
A recoiler that whisks its bearer back to Joppa when triggered, so long as a charged power cell sits inside and no enemy blocks the way. Awarded by Argyve for the first quest
One of the possible player character preset. a True Kin who sets out from Joppa.

A religious order that holds technology itself to be sacred and worships the six Argent Fathers, foremost among them Shekhinah, but also including Reseph. They deem artifacts holy relics unfit for mortal hands, and a breakaway branch venerates the baetyls deep within Bethesda Susa instead.
Giant sentient molluscs of the underground waters, sluggish but immensely strong. Slog of the Cloaca, overlord of the Cloaca in Golgotha, is one of their number.

The Barathrumites' rite of passage: descend the death-pit of Golgotha, recover a scrapped waydroid and repair it while eluding or facing Slog. The reward is Sparafucile's Carbine and access to the Barathrumites' settlement
Humans touched by the mutations of Qud, granted physical or mental powers. They are a playable lineage and the most common kind of mutant met across the world.
The base of the Spindle amid banana groves, holding the Court of the Sultans and the Arcade to the Twin Gates that lead into the Tomb of the Eaters. It is ruled by the self-styled Earl Asphodel.
The urshiib steward of Grit Gate and Barathrum's stern second-in-command. He is the first great quest-giver of the main story.
The only unique member of the fungi faction, hailed by Barathrum as an eccentric mushroom prodigy and a brilliant scientist and engineer. It lives in a hut of mushroom flesh in the Rainbow Wood

Barathrum asks the player to carry the golem climber blueprints to Pax Qlanq and ask him to build it, deep in the Rainbow Wood and reachable only after eating the Eater's flesh. The reward is a quantum mote.
The High Priest of the Mechanimist branch within Bethesda Susa, a boss who no longer recognizes the authority of Eschelstadt II. He leads the faithful of the Temple of the Rock.

A militant order of True Kin purists who loathe every mutant and reserve a special hatred for Barathrum, whom they see as a living rebuke to their creed. They storm Grit Gate and are fought in both A Call to Arms and Reclamation.
A wood of shifting colours filled with slimes and fungi. At its heart grows the Eater's flesh, a fungus that, once eaten, reveals the hidden path to Pax Qlanq's mushroom-flesh hut.
An endgame quest to secure the Spindlegrounds of Omonporch by repelling the Putus Templar and facing Starformed Ehalcodon. .

The seraph known as the Above, a machine-mind within the Seraphic Covenant, remembered as the last Sultan of Qud. From the star-port of Starfarers' Quay he schemes to till the noosphere of all sentient life using the Girsh
The kind of mechanical creatures that walk Qud, untouched by biological mutation.
Crater-like red wells brimming with scrap metal, east of Joppa and threaded with strands of copper wire. The player gathers copper wire here for the opening quest
A legendary True Kin warrior cryogenically frozen in Bethesda Susa. If awaken from his chiliad sleep he will become immediately hostile to the player

The metallic husk of a defunct waydroid, stripped of its copper wire, LED lights and chrome bearings. Found in the Cloaca, it can be repaired into a dormant waydroid to fulfil More Than a Willing Spirit.
Speaking, scheming plants of the Consortium of Phyta, as capable of politics as of photosynthesis. The vainglorious Earl Asphodel springs from this stock.

A covenant bound to the seraphim, orbiting machine-minds orphaned when their Coven abandoned Qud. Reseph, the seraph called the Above, and secretly Barathrum are tied to it, and its purpose is to preserve Qud's life forms
A colossal mollusc that lords over the Cloaca of Golgotha, a legendary boss who spews toxic ooze and crushes its prey beneath its bulk.
An urshiib tinker of Grit Gate, a mid-tier merchant and Barathrumite who keeps the hidden enclave supplied with gear beneath the arch.
A finely made carbine once carried by Sparafucile, weighing 10 and worth 200. It is the reward for completing More Than a Willing Spirit.

A star-port founded by Reseph to receive visitors from across the cosmos, where the ship Exodus lies docked. It is the stage of the quest We Are Starfreight and one of the doorways to the game's several endings.
A star-forged Girsh boss that can be faced during Reclamation by slaying the other six Girsh. Whether it lives or dies opens alternative conversations in the game's epilogue.

A Mechanimist temple set far underground within Bethesda Susa and led by Phinae Hoshaiah. Its breakaway congregation holds the site holy and no longer answers to the High Priest of the distant Six Day Stilt.
Otho charges the player to secure the lease of the Spindle from Asphodel at Omonporch, either by convening a council of allied factions or by striking the self-appointed Earl down.
Barathrum tasks the player with gathering ingredients, neutron flux among them, to construct the Golem. The reward is the Golem itself, the means of ascending the Spindle to reach Starfarers' Quay
Barathrum sends the player to ascend the Tomb of the Eaters and reach Herodododicus, in order to shut down the magnetic field that guards the Spindle. The reward is a vial of metamorphic polygel.
The high-tier merchant role: a trader stocking rare and valuable goods.
The low-tier merchant role: a dealer with a limited, inexpensive stock.
The mid-tier merchant role: a merchant of moderately valuable wares.
The lineage of unmutated humans, the True Kin, whom stable genotype supports cybernetic implants. They are incapable of mutating.
Albino mutant bears clad in quills and blessed with triple-jointed limbs. They are the reclusive tinkers of the Barathrumites, dwelling far below the arch of Grit Gate.
The peaceful farmers of Joppa, the starting village, who tend their watervine along the river. They welcome the fledgling adventurer and stand as the first friendly community of the journey.
The closing quest: reach Reseph at Starfarers' Quay. It leads to the game's ending, where the player forges a covenant with the seraph to evolve Qud's sentient life

The opening quest from Argyve: gather at least 200 feet of copper wire from the Rust Wells and bring it back to build the Weirdwire Conduit. Its reward is a Joppa recoiler and a foothold in the main story.

A high-tier mutant merchant in the Ruined Ward of Bethesda Susa, the one guaranteed seller of neutron flux and a wide array of phials. Speaking with the alchemist for the first time unlocks an achievement. If threatened he will detonate the neutron flux.
A rare applicator from Barathrum's own collection that makes a single exact duplicate of an inventory item before being used up.
An exceedingly rare and volatile liquid that detonates with shattering force ( equal to the weight of a thousand suns) at almost any handling. Incredibly pricy too.

A high-tier floating light source that drifts around its bearer, granting strong resistance to acid, cold, electricity and heat and a bonus to all saving throws. Barathrum gives one to the player after Pax Qlanq, I Presume?.
